title: JSFL: filter management API (getFilters, addFilter, removeFilter, enableFilter, disableFilter)
description:
Add filter management methods to JsflDocument interface + makeDocumentProxy in packages/authoring-ui/src/jsfl/runtime.ts:

1. doc.getFilters(): FlashFilter[] - returns the filters array of the first selected object. Look up the selected object in the current keyframe, return its filters array or [].

2. doc.addFilter(filter: {name: string, [key: string]: any}): void - adds a filter to all selected objects. The filter object has a 'name' field (like 'dropShadow', 'blur', 'glow', 'bevel', 'gradientGlow', 'gradientBevel', 'adjustColor'). Convert to FlashFilter type from @flash/core. Use updateDisplayObject to append to filters array.

3. doc.removeFilter(filterIndex: number): void - removes filter at given index from all selected objects. Use updateDisplayObject to update the filters array.

4. doc.enableFilter(filterIndex: number): void - sets filters[filterIndex].enabled = true on all selected objects.

5. doc.disableFilter(filterIndex: number): void - sets filters[filterIndex].enabled = false on all selected objects.

Look at packages/core/src/engine/filters.ts for the FlashFilter types. The filter 'name' field maps to the type discriminant. For addFilter, map common names: 'dropShadow'->'DropShadow', 'blur'->'Blur', 'glow'->'Glow', etc.
